section_title: What happens when the work is tested?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 10 By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds. 11 For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

12 If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw, 13 his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work. 14 If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward. 15 If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.

context_lines: Paul develops the building picture. By God’s grace he laid the foundation, Jesus Christ, and others are building on it. The warning is to take care how they build. The community is not a project in which every method or teaching is equally sound.

Gold, silver and precious stones are contrasted with wood, hay and straw. The materials picture work whose quality will be exposed. The coming Day will reveal what the builders have done, rather than leaving the judgment to the church’s present admiration for a teacher.

Work that survives receives a reward; work that burns brings loss. Paul says the builder in verse 15 is saved, but as someone escaping through flames. The passage distinguishes the fate of that builder from the fate of the work. This is a serious warning about wasted or harmful contributions, not a reason to treat service as unimportant.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians recognize a warning that God will judge the quality of work built on Christ. Where traditions differ is how this fire relates to purification after death.

The Catholic Church teaches a final purification for those who die in God’s grace but are not yet completely purified. [Catechism 1030–1031 and footnote 605](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P2N.HTM) cite verse 15 among the scriptural references for cleansing fire. This concerns people assured of salvation, rather than a second opportunity to choose salvation after death. Catholic interpretation of this particular passage is not uniform: the [USCCB note on verse 15](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/1corinthians/3) says its immediate subject is not purgatory.

The Reformed [Westminster Confession 32.1](https://www.opc.org/wcf.html) instead teaches that righteous souls are made perfect in holiness and received into heaven at death. [Wesley’s notes on verses 13–15](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-first-epistle-to-the-corinthians/) read the fire as the testing of teaching at the day of judgment and the loss as loss of reward. These readings distinguish testing what someone has built from a period of purification after death.
god_plan_lines: In [Matthew 24:45–47](https://biblehub.com/bsb/matthew/24.htm), Jesus describes a servant entrusted with care for the household while the master is away. The master’s return reveals whether that responsibility has been carried out faithfully.

This is a parallel in accountability, rather than a claim that every detail of the two pictures corresponds. The people entrusted to a servant’s care belong to the Master. Work that truly serves them matters to Him even when public recognition gives an unreliable picture.
current_position_lines: Our study [What Is the True Church?](https://thewayofscripture.com/studies/true-church.html) identifies Christ Himself as the church’s foundation. A teacher, institution or system must serve Him rather than take His place. This is the study’s conclusion about the foundation in verse 11; it does not establish a site conclusion about every detail of the fire and reward in these verses.

editorial_review.position_source_detail: What Is the True Church?, Christ Alone is the Foundation, lines29–37; position limited to3:11, no owner conclusion on fire/purgatory/reward originated.
